title: jig
description: A jig: the unit of configuration and composition. What a runner executes for a project is read from that project's jig. Unrecognised keys are not refused here, because whether an unknown key fails or warns is still open, and a schema that leaves something open leaves it open.

version.description: The version of this format the document claims to conform to, as semver. Optional, and absent means the document claims nothing, which is every document written before this field existed. Present, it lets a consumer refuse a major it does not understand rather than failing later on a field it cannot find.

requires.description: Every executable this jig invokes: the tools its commands run, the adapters its tasks name, any checker it calls. The whole dependency inventory, not a note about unusual tools.

time-limit.description: How long the whole run may take, as a decimal followed by s, m or h. Absent means no limit.
time-limit.$comment: Deliberately narrower than a float parse, so 1e3s, +5s and infs are refused. The grammar and the runner's parser are meant to stay expressible as the same regex, so changing this shape is a decision to make deliberately and to tell the runner about.

definitions.description: Default values for the placeholders this jig's commands name. Optional, and so is any entry in it: a jig leaving a value to its adopter names the placeholder and defines nothing. A definitions file named on the invocation merges over this.

needs-repository-root.description: This jig's commands stand at the repository root rather than at their base. It reaches the working directory and nothing else: the walk, the containment, the filter patterns and {base_dir} all stay what the caller granted. A property of the tool the jig runs rather than of any one caller placing it, so it sits on the jig and not on the jig task.

tasks.description: Executed in declaration order. A task names either a command or a jig, never both.

name.description: Prefixes this task's work directories, so its evidence is identifiable on disk without opening anything. Unique within the jig.

short-circuit-failure.description: Stop the run when this task fails. Stopping is what a jig asks for rather than what it gets.

time-limit.description: How long this task may take, as a decimal followed by s, m or h. Absent means no limit.

command.description: A shell line. How it runs is read off it: {each_path} means one execution per matched path, {all_paths} one execution with the whole selection. Naming both is an error.

optional.description: An empty selection is an acceptable result for this task. Left out, a filtered selection matching nothing is a failure, because a pattern that matches nothing is far more often a stale path than a deliberate one. Only meaningful where a selection exists, so a command naming neither {each_path} nor {all_paths} may not declare it.

adapter.description: Resolved by name from the config directory. Left out, the generic exit-code adapter runs.

adapter-command.description: An explicit adapter invocation, written in place of the default one. The same substitutions are available as in a command, and the envelope is still expected at output.yaml in the work directory, because no flag says where it goes.

evidence.description: The files this task produces that its adapter should read. Declared, never discovered.

jig.description: Retired, and described here so a runner can refuse it by name. Named the jig to run in place of a command, the child following its own requires, tasks and filtering.

in.description: Retired with `jig`. Named a subdirectory of the current base for the child to run in, and was the only thing that set a child's base.

config-dir.description: Retired with `jig`. Named where the child looked for jigs, and was inherited when left out.

output-dir.description: Retired with `jig`. Named the child's output directory, always a subdirectory of this task's work directory.

definitions.description: Retired with `jig`. Named the child's definitions file, as `--definitions` does from the command line, and was inherited when left out.

command.$comment: optional says an empty SELECTION is acceptable, so a command with no selection to be empty cannot declare it. Refused here rather than left to the runner, because it is a property of the jig as written.

oneOf.title: a jig task
oneOf.$comment: Retired, and kept so the refusal comes from the runner. bolt refuses a task carrying `jig` with kind `jig-task-retired` and a message naming the replacement: a command task whose program is bolt, with `adapter: adapters/common/bolt-result.py` reading the child's result. Removing this branch makes such a task fail `'command' is a required property`, which names neither the cause nor the fix, and the runner never reaches its own message. Measured against a jig carrying all five fields.

pathList.description: Patterns or literal paths, relative to the base of the run they are declared in, where ** matches zero or more directory levels.
